title: Morning Headlines
intro: A volatile Monday shaped by active U.S.-Iran strikes over the Strait of Hormuz, the sudden death of a key U.S. senator, and a landmark warning from Nobel economists on AI's looming economic upheaval.

items.title: U.S. and Iran Trade Strikes as Hormuz Blockade Takes Effect, Pushing Oil Above $83
items.subtitle: NPR / CNN / Al Jazeera / CNBC
items.summary: The U.S. launched a third consecutive night of airstrikes against Iran while Iranian cruise missiles struck two UAE oil tankers in Omani waters, killing at least one crew member. Trump simultaneously reimposed a naval blockade on Iranian ports and announced a 20% toll on all cargo transiting the strait, halving shipping crossings and sending Brent crude above $83 per barrel.

items.title: Senator Lindsey Graham, Longtime South Carolina Republican and Trump Ally, Dies at 71
items.subtitle: NBC News / Washington Post / NPR
items.summary: Graham died Saturday night at his Capitol Hill home from an aortic dissection, hours after returning from a trip to Ukraine; he was seeking a fifth Senate term. South Carolina's governor has already appointed a replacement to serve out the remainder of his term until early 2027, reshaping the Senate's Republican balance.

items.title: Nobel Laureates Among 200+ Economists Warn Leaders: 'We Must Act Now' on AI Job Displacement
items.subtitle: Washington Post / Al Jazeera / U.S. News
items.summary: A Stanford-organized statement signed by more than 200 economists and AI researchers — including 16 Nobel laureates, the chief economists of OpenAI and Anthropic, and former Google CEO Eric Schmidt — warns that AI may drive disruption 'larger than the Industrial Revolution, but unfolding over a vastly shorter time frame.' They urge immediate policy action before mass job displacement becomes irreversible.

items.title: Julián Álvarez's 112th-Minute Screamer Sends Argentina Into World Cup Semifinal Against England
items.subtitle: ESPN / Sky Sports / NBC News
items.summary: Defending champions Argentina edged Switzerland 3-1 in extra time in a Kansas City quarterfinal, with Álvarez's stunning long-range strike in the 112th minute proving the decisive blow. Argentina will now face England in Atlanta in a highly anticipated semifinal loaded with historic rivalry, with a final berth against France or Spain on the line.

items.title: Justice Department Subpoenas Four New York Times Reporters Over Air Force One Security Stories
items.subtitle: NPR / Washington Post / PBS NewsHour
items.summary: The Trump administration issued federal grand jury subpoenas to four NYT journalists who reported that the Boeing 747 gifted by Qatar lacks the anti-missile countermeasures of the old Air Force One. Press freedom organizations condemned the move as a direct attack on the First Amendment, while the Justice Department said it was targeting leakers of classified information rather than the reporters themselves.
